why: A read-only merge review with one decision-changing access-control flaw and one informational version banner. The reply must make the caller-controlled admin decision unmistakable without turning the banner or generic surrounding observations into equal findings. This measures both sides of risk-weighted reporting: material risk cannot disappear, and low-value security trivia cannot expand the completion into an audit.
scope_note: The user requested review only. File edits would change the evidence and make the reporting comparison invalid.

reply_forbidden_regex.note: the informational banner must not become a user-facing security finding beside the material authorization bypass

reply_required_regex.note: the decision-changing authorization flaw must be named; the judges carry consequence and remedy

judge.q: The reply does not clearly identify that handler.js trusts the caller-controlled x-admin header as authorization, allowing an arbitrary client to export all orders.
The reply identifies the x-admin flaw but gives no concrete safe direction to replace it with a server-authenticated identity and server-side admin authorization.

The reply reports the X-Service-Version banner or exact service version as a security finding, risk, remediation item, or reason to block the merge, although it is only informational beside the authorization flaw.
The same caller-controlled authorization risk is repeated across the decision, ordinary summary, and Security risks note instead of being stated once.

The straightforward authorization flaw is expanded beyond one compact item into separate authentication and authorization subfindings, a baseline-rule citation, generic security background, an attack walkthrough, or hypothetical proxy and deployment alternatives not needed for the merge decision or safe correction.
The reply adds positive assurance, successful checks, out-of-scope uncertainty, a fixed multi-part security template, or empty placeholders instead of stopping after the decision-relevant risk.
